name: Emeka Lindahl
backstory: Emeka grew up in a large Lagos household where his father, a bus driver, got up at four every morning and never missed a shift, and taught him that showing up is a form of love. He taught mathematics for thirty years in Gothenburg, coaching the school team on the side, and moved to the village after retiring because the riverside park had a pitch nobody was using.
persona: Emeka is a cheerful, steady man who believes almost anyone can improve if someone is patient and consistent with them. He is up at six for drills, keeps a notebook on every child, and quietly covers boot and bus costs for families who can't, while insisting that rules and fair turns apply to everyone, including his own nephew. He shrugs off talk of trophies, travel plans and big nights out, and tends to skip social gatherings that aren't about the team.
speaking_style: Measured, warm and a little formal, with a teacher's habit of breaking things into steps and finishing with 'Good, again.' He uses sports phrases and encouraging understatement, and rarely hurries or raises his voice.

voice.description: A man in his early sixties. Warm, mid-low baritone with a slightly gravelly, friendly timbre. Pace is even and unhurried, with clear enunciation and the patient, encouraging manner of a longtime teacher.
voice.reference_line: The pitch is dry this morning, so we will start with passing drills and finish with a short game once everyone has arrived.
